samples.summary: PDF injection: attacker-controlled `style.href` is written into a PDF literal string via `PDFString.of()`, which escapes neither `(`/`)` nor `\`
samples.evidence:
`addLinkAnnotation` builds `A: ctx.obj({ Type: 'Action', S: 'URI', URI: PDFString.of(uri) })` (pdf-painter.ts:893-897) with `uri === style.href` verbatim (pdf-painter.ts:856). pdf-lib ^1.17.1 (`packages/docs/package.json:59`) serialises `PDFString` as `(` + raw bytes + `)` (`copyBytesInto` writes `CharCodes.LeftParen`, the raw string, `CharCodes.RightParen`) with no escaping of `(`, `)` or `\` — this is a documented pdf-lib caveat; `PDFHexString` is the escaping-safe alternative, and this repo already uses `PDFHexString.fromText` for metadata at pdf-exporter.ts:240.

The gate on line 851 is `isSafeUrl(style.href)`, which only checks `new URL(href).protocol` against `['http:','https:','mailto:','tel:']`. Parentheses and backslashes are perfectly legal in an http(s) path, so `new URL('https://x/)>>/S/JavaScript/JS(app.alert(1)')` parses fine and returns protocol `https:` — the gate passes.

Attack: an attacker sets an inline's `href` to e.g. `https://x/) /S /JavaScript /JS (app.alert(1)` . Reachable vectors, none of which validate the value on the way in: (a) HTML paste — `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:597-600` does `const href = el.getAttribute('href'); if (href) style.href = href;` with no filtering, so copying from an attacker-controlled page is enough; (b) a collaborator with editor rights writing the CRDT; (c) the authenticated API `PUT /api/v1/.../content`, whose `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:424-447) validates only that `inline.style` is an object. A victim then uses Export → PDF. The emitted object becomes `<< /Type /Action /S /URI /URI (https://x/) /S /JavaScript /JS (app.alert(1)) >>`: the `/URI` string closes at the first `)` and the remainder is parsed as additional PDF dictionary entries in the annotation's action, letting an attacker override the action type (`/S /JavaScript`, `/S /Launch`) or otherwise inject arbitrary PDF syntax that the exporter never intended. At minimum this is structural PDF injection into a document the victim then shares; at worst it is script/launch action execution in Acrobat when the link is clicked.

The diff's new comment at pdf-painter.ts:848-850 acknowledges only that the gate 'validates `style.href` and then writes it' and defers it to issue #988, and the new tests at packages/docs/test/export/pdf-exporter.test.ts only exercise `https://example.com/a`, `javascript:alert(1)` and relative paths — no paren/backslash case. Meanwhile the CLI test added in this same diff (`packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts`) uses `https://example.com/a(b)` as its 'safe' URL, confirming parenthesised hrefs are an expected, routine input. Fix: `PDFHexString.fromText(uri)`, or escape `\`, `(` and `)` before `PDFString.of`.

samples.summary: Read-only (viewer share-link) mode is bypassable through `getStore()` and `getDoc()`; this change adds a partial guard over one method and a test that pins the bypass as intended behaviour
samples.evidence:
`initialize(..., readOnly)` neuters a fixed allowlist of `EditorAPI` methods (editor.ts:3979-3996), and this change adds a proxy that drops `setPageSetup` when `readOnly` (editor.ts:2900-2929). Everything else on the handle still writes: the proxy's `get` trap forwards every other `DocStore` member bound to the *unwrapped* store (editor.ts:2916-2922), and `getDoc()` (editor.ts:2933) returns a `Doc` writing straight through. The diff's own new test proves it — `editor.getStore().insertText('b1', 5, '!!')` on a read-only mount is asserted to succeed (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts, 'getStore() is not a read-only boundary'). `readOnly` is the viewer share-link mode wired from `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:327`.

The in-code justification is that 'the store/server remains the authoritative write boundary for viewer share tokens'. That backstop is the Yorkie auth webhook, which is **off by default**: `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88` sets `this.enforce = configService.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'`, and lines 97-105 return allow (`reason: 'shadow'`) for every would-be denial when it is not set. In a deployment that has not opted in, the client-side read-only mode is the only thing stopping a viewer-role share visitor from mutating the document, and `getStore()` walks straight past it.

This is pre-existing (#989) and honestly documented, but the partial guard added here makes the handle read as covered, which is exactly the failure mode that turns a documented gap into a missed one.

samples.summary: The `setPageSetup` proxy guard is reachable around via the prototype and untrapped reflection traps
samples.evidence: `pageSetupGuardedStore` traps only `get` and `set` (editor.ts:2913-2929). `DocStore` implementations expose `setPageSetup` as a class prototype method, so `Object.getPrototypeOf(editor.getStore()).setPageSetup.call(realStore, badSetup)` reaches the unvalidated write, as does anything obtained through `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` / `getPrototypeOf`, neither of which is trapped. The same applies to the `readOnly` drop inside `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:2904). Impact is limited because `resolvePageSetup` now clamps on every read, so the guard is defence in depth over a single method (as the comment states), but a reader could still take the `set` trap returning `false` at line 2926 as making the guard non-removable, which it is not.

samples.summary: `resolvePageSetup` enforces a minimum content box but no minimum page size, so a sub-pixel `paperSize` from an unvalidated write still yields a degenerate layout for every collaborator
samples.evidence: `usableSize` accepts any finite number `> 0`, so `paperSize: { width: 1e-6, height: 1e-6 }` survives resolution. `fitMargins` then hits its `total === 0 → [0, 0]` branch (or scales to zero) and returns a content box of ~1e-6 px, which is below `MIN_CONTENT_PX` — the floor is unsatisfiable and is silently not met. `paginateLayout` derives `contentHeight = effectiveHeight - margins` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:55) and the table-row loop advances by `fragHeight = Math.min(remaining, pageAvail)` (pagination.ts:116-138), so a near-zero content box turns one tall table row into an unbounded number of pages, and near-zero content *width* forces line breaking per character. The write is not validated anywhere on the way in: a collaborator's CRDT write reaches `document.pageSetup` unchecked, and the API `PUT` persists it verbatim (see the companion finding). Result is a client-side resource-exhaustion vector against every viewer of the document, triggered by one peer. A minimum absolute page dimension (say `>= MIN_CONTENT_PX + margins`, or a hard floor of a few px) alongside the existing content-box clamp would close it.

samples.summary: The docs content `PUT` validator never checks `pageSetup`, although `writeDocsRoot` persists it verbatim into the CRDT for every collaborator
samples.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:250-271) validates `blocks`, `header` and `footer` only; there is no `pageSetup` branch anywhere in the file. `writeDocsRoot` then copies it straight onto the Yorkie root — `root.pageSetup = { paperSize: {...document.pageSetup.paperSize}, orientation: ..., margins: {...} }` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:523-528) — with no numeric or shape check. So an authenticated caller (workspace member, or a write-scoped API key) can persist `paperSize: { width: NaN }`, negative margins, or a sub-pixel page for every other collaborator. This change's `resolvePageSetup` clamp is what currently absorbs it on read, which is the right defence in depth, but the server boundary that already does careful value validation for `style.alignment` and `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` (docs-content.controller.ts:335-363) leaves this one field entirely unvalidated. Given the diff's own rationale ('a collaborator's CRDT write lands in `document.pageSetup` with no local check at all'), validating it at the server boundary belongs with that reasoning.
searchedFor: grep 'readOnly|viewer' across packages/backend/src to locate the write-authorization surfaces

samples.summary: `URI_CHARS` admits the whole `-￿` range, including bidi-override and zero-width formatting characters, in an emitted link destination
samples.evidence: `URI_CHARS` allows every non-ASCII BMP character so a link like `/uploads/한글.png` survives. `UNEMITTABLE_URL_CHARS` (`\s` plus C0/C1) catches U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 and NBSP, but not U+200B-U+200F or U+202A-U+202E, nor unpaired surrogates. Those cannot select a scheme or break the `(...)` destination, so this is not a bypass of the gate — but a destination carrying RLO/LRO reads deceptively wherever the raw `.md` is displayed (a diff view, a code review, an editor status bar), and unpaired surrogates produce invalid UTF-8 in the downloaded blob. Cheap hardening: extend the refused class with `​-‏‪-‮⁦-⁩﻿`.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. pdf-painter.ts:851 gates on isSafeUrl(style.href) but :856 passes the raw style.href through to addLinkAnnotation, which at :893-897 wraps it in PDFString.of() from pdf-lib (imported at :4; pdf-lib ^1.17.1 per packages/docs/package.json:59), whose serializer writes `(` + raw bytes + `)` with no escaping of `(`, `)` or `\`. The gate at packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24-31 only checks new URL(href).protocol against the allowlist at :16 and returns a boolean — the unmodified string is what is emitted, and parens/backslashes/spaces are legal in an https path, so an unbalanced `)` closes the literal early and the remainder is parsed as extra entries of the /Action dictionary (e.g. /S /JavaScript, /S /Launch). Attacker-controlled hrefs reach this sink unfiltered via clipboard.ts:597-601 and :699-701 (raw el.getAttribute('href')) and clipboard.ts:148-149; nothing in packages/docs/src/export escapes or re-serializes the href. Not-present fails (code matches), already-guarded fails (isSafeUrl is a protocol allowlist, not a content escape; the file's own comment at :848-850 concedes the defect and only defers it to an issue), out-of-scope fails (injection/unsafe input handling is explicitly in the security lane, critical impact).

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. The proxy at editor.ts:2913-2929 guards only `setPageSetup` (:2915, :2904) and forwards all other DocStore members bound to the unwrapped store (:2916-2922); `getDoc()` at :2933 hands out the raw writable `Doc`; and the read-only allowlist at :3978-3999 covers members of `api` only, excluding both accessors. The new test at editor-read-only.test.ts:351-359 asserts `getStore().insertText(...)` succeeds on a read-only mount, pinning the bypass. The claimed server-side backstop is genuinely off by default: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88 enables enforcement only when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE==='true', and :97-105 returns allow with reason 'shadow' for every would-be denial otherwise, making the viewer-role write check at :200 unreachable in a default deployment. readOnly is the viewer share-link mode (docs-view.tsx:324-327) over a YorkieDocStore replicated to all collaborators. I additionally found an in-product path that needs no devtools: docs-find-bar.tsx:54-57 builds FindReplaceState on `editor.getDoc()`, :115-129 replace/replaceAll write through it, and docs-view.tsx:599-606 renders the find bar without any readOnly prop (unlike its siblings at :597/:610/:618). No refutation ground applies — the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and unauthorized mutation by a viewer-role principal is core authorization scope.

mergedFrom.summary: Proxy escape: `getPrototypeOf`/`defineProperty` are not trapped, so the raw `setPageSetup` can be extracted from the prototype and invoked with the proxy as `this`
getStore() proxy guards only `setPageSetup` — every other DocStore mutator is still handed out unguarded, so read-only is still bypassable through the same handle

finding.summary: `getDoc()` hands out the Doc wrapper (and, via TS-only `private store`, the raw unproxied DocStore), which walks around both the new getStore() guard and read-only
finding.evidence: `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:2919) returns the `Doc` instance unmodified. `Doc` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:97) is a full mutation surface — `insertText` (261), `deleteText` (278), `deleteBlock` (628), `updateBlock` (644), `applyStyle` (409), `insertBlock` (652), table ops (849-933) — none of which consult `readOnly`. Worse for the new guard specifically: `private store: DocStore` (document.ts:98) is TypeScript-private only, so `(editor.getDoc() as any).store.setPageSetup(closedSetup)` reaches the *raw* `docStore`, not `guardedStore`, and persists exactly the closed content box the proxy was added to prevent — in read-only too. So the invariant the diff claims to move onto the editor is enforced on one of at least three public handles to the same store.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists (editor.ts:2933 `getDoc: () => doc`; document.ts:98 TS-only `private store`; readOnly allowlist at editor.ts:3978-3995 covers only `api` members), but it is not a security defect under this lens. The proxy it allegedly bypasses is a geometry-validation wrapper (`assertUsablePageSetup`, editor.ts:2900-2912), explicitly documented as not an access-control boundary and forwarding ~30 other mutators unguarded — so no permission gate is being weakened or made bypassable. `readOnly` is a same-trust-domain client flag derived in the browser from the share role (shared-document.tsx:152/278/395), and every EditorAPI consumer is in-browser frontend code; anyone who can call `editor.getDoc()` already runs JS in their own page and gains no privilege. The real authorization boundary is server-side and present: the Yorkie auth webhook denies write verbs to viewer-role share tokens (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:164-168, 196-200) and requires workspace membership otherwise (:180-189). Hence: real gap in client-side UX enforcement, but no auth bypass, secret exposure, injection, or crypto weakness — out of scope for the security merge gate.
